title: Nilpotent derived reduction detects an upper cohomological bound
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$, $C\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and $b\in\mathbf Z$. Put $\overline C=C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}A/I$ using derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] on the one-object site with only the identity covering. If $H^i(\overline C)=0$ for every $i>b$, then $H^i(C)=0$ for every $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, upper-bound-only version of its nilpotent filtration proof, as used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Work on the one-object site with identity covering, where sheaves of A-modules are ordinary A-modules. Choose a representing complex G for C, and use [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] to obtain a quasi-isomorphism P → G with P K-flat and every P^r flat. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], Q=P⊗_A B, where B=A/I, represents the given reduced object. By [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], Q is K-flat over B and has flat B-module terms. In particular H^i(Q)=0 for i>b, without assuming P bounded.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, nilpotent filtration proof; upper-bound-only adaptation used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Form the good truncation T of Q: T^r=Q^r for r<b, T^b=ker(d_Q^b), and T^r=0 for r>b. The inclusion T→Q induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at most b; above b both cohomologies vanish. Thus it is a quasi-isomorphism by direct calculation of kernels and images. Apply [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement] over B with N=b to obtain F→T with F^r=0 for r>b, all terms flat, and F→T a quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], F is K-flat. The composite α:F→Q is a quasi-isomorphism between K-flat B-complexes.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, nilpotent filtration proof; upper-bound-only adaptation used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: For every B-module M, the cone E=Cone(α) is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] and K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum]. Regard M as a complex concentrated in degree zero. By [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary], M⊗_B E is acyclic. The degreewise maps m⊗e ↦ e⊗m and e⊗m ↦ m⊗e are inverse balanced maps commuting with differentials: the differential on the degree-zero M factor is zero, so both tensor differentials act only on e and no sign is introduced. Hence E⊗_B M is acyclic as well. The degreewise distributivity isomorphism identifies this with Cone(α⊗1_M): the differentials are the same block matrix with entries d_Q⊗1, α⊗1, and −d_F⊗1. The cone criterion again proves F⊗_B M→Q⊗_B M is a quasi-isomorphism. Since F⊗_B M is zero in degrees greater than b, H^i(Q⊗_B M)=0 for i>b. This establishes the upper tensor bound needed below; no lower bound or finite Tor amplitude is inferred.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, nilpotent filtration proof; upper-bound-only adaptation used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: If M is an A-module with IM=0, give it its quotient B-module structure. There is an isomorphism of complexes P⊗_A M≅(P⊗_A B)⊗_B M=Q⊗_B M. Explicitly p⊗m maps to (p⊗1)⊗m, with inverse (p⊗ā)⊗m ↦ p⊗am; the inverse is independent of the lift a because I kills M. These formulas respect balanced tensor relations and commute with the differential d_P. The preceding step therefore proves H^i(P⊗_A M)=0 for i>b whenever IM=0.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, nilpotent filtration proof; upper-bound-only adaptation used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Induct on t≥1 to show that every A-module M killed by I^t has H^i(P⊗_A M)=0 for i>b. The case t=1 is the preceding step. If I^{t+1}M=0, then I^t(IM)=0 and I(M/IM)=0. The sequence 0→IM→M→M/IM→0 is short exact. By flatness of every P^r, in precisely the exact-functor sense of [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], tensoring it with P gives a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes. The induction hypothesis and the base case give the bound for its first and third complexes. Here is the required middle exactness argument, rather than an uncited appeal to a long exact sequence: for a degree i>b cocycle z in P⊗M, its image in P⊗(M/IM) is dy since that cohomology vanishes. Lift y to degree i−1 of P⊗M; z−dy comes from an element x of degree i in P⊗IM. Injectivity in degree i+1 shows dx=0. Write x=dw using vanishing of H^i(P⊗IM). Then z=d(y+w) after including w in P⊗M. Every such cocycle is a boundary, completing the induction.

source.place: Tag 0H75, lemma-check-tor-dimension-modulo-nilpotent, nilpotent filtration proof; upper-bound-only adaptation used by Tag 09AR

proof.text: Apply the induction with t=N and M=A, since I^N A=0. The complex P⊗_A A is isomorphic to P via p⊗a ↦ ap, with inverse p ↦ p⊗1. Thus H^i(P)=0 for all i>b. Since P→G is a quasi-isomorphism and G represents C, the same vanishing holds for C.

lean.statement: theorem isZero_homology_of_nilpotent_derived_reduction {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (hI : I ^ N = ⊥) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I))] (E : RingSiteModules A ⥤ RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I)) (hobjects : ∀ M : RingSiteModules A, E.obj M = SheafOfModules.changeOfRings (ringSiteMap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) M) (hmaps : ∀ {M M' : RingSiteModules A} (f : M ⟶ M'), E.map f = eqToHom (hobjects M) ≫ SheafOfModules.changeOfRingsHom (ringSiteMap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)) M f ≫ eqToHom (hobjects M').symm) [E.Additive] (LF : DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules A) ⥤ DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I))) (ε : Qh ⋙ LF ⟶ E.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ Qh) (hLF : LF.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (RingSiteModules A) (ComplexShape.up ℤ))) (C : DerivedCategory (RingSiteModules A)) (b : ℤ) (hred : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((homologyFunctor (RingSiteModules (A ⧸ I)) i).obj (LF.obj C))) : ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((homologyFunctor (RingSiteModules A) i).obj C)
